title: Idempotent provisioning kit for Private EKS control plane - Terraform bootstrap & health playbook
creator: Ethan Lewis
description:
Goal: Ship an idempotent, operatorless Terraform module and companion bootstrap playbook to safely provision and upgrade Redwood Private EKS control planes inside customer VPCs. This ticket covers: the Terraform module API, preflight and postflight health probes, immutable bootstrap flow (canary plan/apply + staged promotion), S3 state lock and short TTL safety net, and an automated smoke-test harness that runs after each apply.

Scope (what this module provides):
- Module entrypoint: redwood_priv_eks_controlplane
- Resources: EKS control plane (managed), control plane IAM roles, cross-account KMS key alias wiring, cluster endpoint private access settings, cluster logging config, control-plane security groups, nodebootstrap submodule integration points (not creating nodes by default).
- State handling: opinionated S3 backend patterns and DynamoDB lock TTLs with promptable lock-override in emergencies.
- Preflight validations: VPC/subnet reachability, ENI quota checks, KMS key policy sanity, required IAM permissions checks via dry-run assume-role.
- Health checks: integrated controlplane-prober job (lambda/step-function) that runs kube-apiserver readiness checks, cert rotation status, and kube-controller-manager control-plane metrics via Prometheus exporter.
- Upgrade strategy: plan-only canaries (terraform plan -> dry-run apply in isolated test account), staged apply with maintenance window enforcement, snapshot-before-upgrade (Velero/etcd snapshot recommended) and automated rollback runbook.
- Observability: emit provisioning metrics to central telemetry (datapoint names and labels in docs), and create a dashboard template in Grafana for provisioning runs (latency, failures, drift).
- CI integration: terraform fmt/validate/plan gating in infra repo; post-apply smoke tests run in GH Actions and publish artifacts to Drive/Confluence; acceptance harness includes kubeconformance-lite and a simple cert issuance test.

Non-goals: Node lifecycle management, full operator controller creation (we avoid long-running control-plane operators in this module), and data plane autoscaling policies (handled elsewhere).

Acceptance criteria:
- Module published to infra/terraform-modules with semver and README including variables/outputs/examples.
- Happy-path provisioning smoke test passes in staging account with shared CI job.
- Preflight checks detect and block known quota and KMS misconfigurations.
- Canary plan/apply workflow documented and runnable by SRE/SE.
- Health probe Lambda/step-function emits consistent metrics and a dashboard template exists.

Examples & snippets (to include in README):
1) Minimal use:
module "redwood_priv_eks" {
  source = "github.com/redwood-inference/infra//modules/redwood_priv_eks_controlplane?ref=v0.1.0"
  name   = "redwood-priv-cluster-${var.env}"
  vpc_id = var.vpc_id
  private_subnet_ids = var.private_subnet_ids
  kms_key_alias = "alias/redwood-priv-${var.account_id}"
  enable_control_plane_logging = true
}

2) Canary plan workflow (CI):
- run: terraform init -backend-config=canary-backend.hcl
- run: terraform plan -out=canary.plan
- run: terraform apply -auto-approve canary.plan 
- run: ./tools/post_apply_smoketest.sh --cluster ${CANARY_CLUSTER}

Related artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFRAPUB/pages/Priv+EKS+Bootstrap+Kit
- Proposal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123
- Prototype module (branch): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/tree/priv-eks-bootstrapper
- Grafana template (drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-example-dashboard

Notes on safety and drift: We introduce a manifest-level drift guard that runs terraform plan and rejects applies when changes touch a denylist (eg. vpc/cidr/classic-load-balancer removal). We also add a controlled 'terraform apply --target=policy_exceptions' path to capture emergency moves with explicit human approval recorded in the run metadata.
